items.actClause: AN ACT to amend part LL-1 of chapter 57 of the laws of 2008, relating to directing the commissioner of taxation and finance to institute a re-registration program, in relation to prohibiting the New York state department of taxation and finance from charging a vendor re-registration fee; and to amend the tax law, in relation to prohibiting the New York state department of taxation and finance from charging vendors any fees to collect NYS sales tax
items.lawCode: Amd Part LL-1 §1, Chap 57 of 2008; amd §1134, Tax L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S203                REVISED MEMO 02/24/2017

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend part LL-1 of chapter 57 of the laws
of 2008, relating to directing the commissioner of taxation and
finance to institute a re-registration program, in relation to
prohibiting the New York state department of taxation and finance from
charging a vendor re-registration fee; and to amend the tax law, in
relation to prohibiting the New York state department of taxation and
finance from charging vendors any fees to collect NYS sales tax

 PURPOSE :

To prohibit the New York state department of taxation and finance from
charging a fee for applications for a certificate of registration
pursuant to a re-registration program.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section one amends Section 1 of part LL-1 of chapter 57 of the laws of
2008 to eliminate the re-registration fee required to be paid by those
people required to file sales and compensating use tax returns.

Section two amends paragraph 5 of subdivision (a) of section 1134 of
the tax law to prohibit the New York State Department of Taxation and
Finance from charging vendors any fees to collect New York State sales
tax.

Section three establishes the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

New York State must become more business friendly by providing
businesses with opportunities to succeed. The 2008 "Vendor
Registration Fee is another disincentive to own and operate a business
in New York State. The original certificate of registration to collect
sales tax for the New York State Department of Taxation and Finance
was issued to businesses with no fees and no expiration date. Business
in the state should not have to pay for the privilege of collecting
state sales tax. The current law does not indicate that this is a
one-time fee and many business owners are leery that this will become
another revenue stream for the state on an ongoing basis and fees
could increase as time goes on. This bill would prevent the New York
State Department of Taxation and Finance from charging a registration
fee for vendors to collect sales tax.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

2016: Committed to Finance

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

Per the Department of Taxation and Finance, "this proposal would have
no fiscal impact on State revenues in SFY 2017-18 or in subsequent
fiscal years".

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediately.

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S203A

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the tax law, in relation to prohibiting the New York
state department of taxation and finance from charging vendors any
fees to collect NYS sales tax; and to repeal section 1 of part LL-1 of
chapter 57 of the laws of 2008, relating to directing the commissioner
of taxation and finance to institute a re-registration program

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section one repeals Section 1 of part LL-1 of chapter 57 of the laws
of 2008 as the program it authorizes no longer exists.

Section two amends paragraph 5 of subdivision (a) of section 1134 of
the tax law to prohibit the New York State Department of Taxation and
Finance from charging vendors any fees to collect New York State sales
tax.

Section three establishes the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

New York State must become more business friendly by providing busi-
nesses with opportunities to succeed. The original certificate of
registration to collect sales tax for the New York State Department of
Taxation and Finance was issued to businesses with no fees and no
expiration date. This bill would prevent the New York State Department
of Taxation and Finance from charging a registration fee for vendors
to collect sales tax by specifically specifying that these types of
certificates of registration be issued without charge.  Business in
the state should not have to pay for the privilege of collecting state
sales tax.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

2016: Committed to Finance

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

Per the Department of Taxation and Finance, "this proposal would have
no fiscal impact on State revenues in SFY 2017-18 or in subsequent
fiscal years".

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediately.
